title: Round 10 Post Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 press conference following the Sprint Race at Monza. Joining us are third-placed Oliver Goethe of MP Motorsport, second-placed John Bennett of TRIDENT, and race winner Joshua Duerksen of Invicta Racing. Joshua, congratulations. How does that win feel?

Joshua Duerksen: It was an amazing race. Winning at Monza is always special. The car was very strong, I made a good start and that helped me move forward early. The pace was good throughout and I am very happy we were able to bring home the victory.

FIA Formula 2: The car looked very well set up. How does that prepare you for the Feature Race?

Duerksen: We gathered a lot of useful data. We learned about the car in traffic and in clean air, and we now have a very good picture of what we need for tomorrow.

FIA Formula 2: What are your thoughts on the new 2027 FIA Formula 2 car unveiled today?

Duerksen: I really like it. The front and rear wings look much closer to Formula 1 and I am curious to see how it races next year.

FIA Formula 2: John, congratulations on P2, your second podium of the season. How was the race from your perspective?

John Bennett: We were targeting the win from pole position, but I am still satisfied with a podium. We built a gap at the front before the first Safety Car, but Joshua was simply too quick. The pace and tyre management were strong, so another podium is a good feeling.

FIA Formula 2: How much tyre management was required?

Bennett: Monza requires less tyre saving than many circuits. We were pushing fairly hard, particularly in clean air, but still trying to look after the rear tyres.

FIA Formula 2: Your thoughts on the new 2027 car?

Bennett: It looks fantastic. Visually it is much more in line with Formula 1 today.

FIA Formula 2: Ollie, starting from the front row, you seemed to spend much of the race attacking and defending. How challenging was that?

Oliver Goethe: It was a difficult race. I put myself in a few bad positions and lost places, so it was not ideal. Even so, I recovered to third and another podium, which I am happy with.

FIA Formula 2: What do you think of the 2027 car?

Goethe: I agree with the others. It looks cool and much more like Formula 1.

title: Van Hoepen happy with recovery effort and TRIDENT pace after Sprint Race points
excerpt:
Laurens van Hoepen was able to recover from a tough Qualifying result on Friday at Monza to rebound into the points in Saturday’s Sprint.

The TRIDENT driver went from 15th on the grid, but by the time the chequered flag was waving to end the first race of the weekend, he sat P8 and claimed a hard-earned points.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, the Dutch driver says that he was very pleased to show the team’s true pace, and that the pace in the Sprint bodes well for what’s to come in the Feature Race on Sunday.

“I think it was a good recovery from yesterday,” van Hoepen said. “It was a tough qualifying to then gain seven positions, score at least one point in the Sprint Race. It's always a bit more tricky to gain positions in the Sprint compared to the Features.

READ MORE

SPRINT RACE: Duerksen charges through from seventh to win at Monza

"It's promising for tomorrow. I think we definitely have some stuff to work on still, but we're going to look into the data and see where we can improve, and then hopefully gain even more positions tomorrow.”

Van Hoepen kept himself out of trouble in a race where several of his rivals around him nearly came to blows.

The TRIDENT driver said that it was his game plan to assess things after the start and keep his nose clean. From there, he said that it was about managing the tyres, with the temperatures in Monza making tyre preservation a crucial element in the Sprint.

Van Hoepen is eyeing up another charge through the pack on Sunday in the Feature Race

"As a team we managed the race quite well. I had a good start and then kind of tried to stay a bit out of trouble and not to do too many mistakes. I also took care not to overheat the tyres, because that was a big factor, because it's so hot on track the tyres really are screaming at some point. So I tried to manage that, and honestly, it looked like we were quick in the corners.

“We were sliding a bit less than the other guys at the end, so that, I think, just helped. And then we had some life left at the end of the race. I think maybe it would have been a bit better if there was no Safety Car at the end but tomorrow is the main race and we’ll go for it again.”

With the higher points on offer in the Feature Race on Sunday, van Hoepen is optimistic of his chances in repeating his charge up the order.

He added that with the unpredictable nature of Monza, anything could happen and that he will be targeting another haul of points to take home from Italy.

“Yesterday was, I would say, was my fault. So I was really upset with that, it just makes the weekend a whole lot tougher.

“But at least we recovered today, and we still have one more race to go that we can fully recover the weekend. The strategy here is always a bit similar in a sense, but the Safety Car can play a part. It's just about making sure you're ready for everything.

"We have some data from the past couple of years, and there's always so much chaos happening at Monza that you just have to be prepared for everything. Then it’s about taking any opportunity that comes to you.”

title: SPRINT RACE: Duerksen charges through from seventh to win at Monza
excerpt:
Invicta Racing’s Joshua Duerksen put in a stellar drive from the fourth row on the grid to win the Sprint Race from P7.

The Paraguayan driver controlled a late-race Safety Car restart to earn his third Sprint of the 2026 season and in the process became the driver with the most podiums at Monza in F2.

TRIDENT’s John Bennett claimed P2 in what was his 50th start, while Oliver Goethe completed the podium in third place for MP Motorsport.

AS IT HAPPENED

Reverse grid pole sitter Bennett covered off Goethe to retain the lead into Turn 1, and that allowed Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak to take second position at the first chicane.

Behind them, Duerksen was on the charge and up to fourth, rounding Martinius Stenshorne into the first Lesmo.

Lap 2 and Nikola Tsolov took sixth place from Ritomo Miyata into the final corner. Up ahead and opening the third tour, Duerksen took third place from Goethe, who then also lost a spot to Stenshorne on the run to Turn 4. Their battling had allowed leader Bennett to escape two seconds up the road and well out of DRS range to those behind.

Duerksen tried to fight around the outside of Inthraphuvasak at the first corner to begin Lap 4 but the Paraguayan driver had to cut across the corner, staying third for the time being.

Championship leader Tsolov lost out to Campos Racing teammate Noel León on traction exiting the second chicane, dropping the Bulgarian back down to seventh.

Lap 5 and Duerksen nailed a DRS pass to take second position from Inthraphuvasak.

In the title fight, it was a dramatic few corners as Alexander Dunne and Tsolov went wheel-to-wheel in the opening chicane but ran deep into Turn 2, dropping them down to eighth and ninth places.

Right behind them, Feature Race pole sitter Rafael Câmara was spun around after contact with Nico Varrone on corner exit and stalled. This left him out of the running having been on the cusp of the points places. The Safety Car was then deployed to recover the stationary Invicta car.

Bennett launched back to racing conditions at the start of Lap 7 and he kept Duerksen at bay into the first corners.

León continued his progress as he cleared Stenshorne into the final corner to take fifth position, though the Norwegian fought back through at the first corner on the following lap.

Duerksen was glued to the rear wing of Bennett and with DRS, the Invicta driver claimed the lead of the race on Lap 9 into Turn 1.

A slight error through Ascari left Goethe under pressure from Stenshorne entering Lap 11, and with a tow from Inthraphuvasak ahead, the Rodin driver moved into P4.

Lap 12 and a lock-up at Turn 1 sent Inthraphuvasak across the escape road, dropping him from third to fifth. León then took advantage to dive down the outside at Turn 4 and demote the Thai driver to P6.

Tsolov claimed the place on the following lap, moving down the inside of the ART driver at the first corner. Dunne then pulled off a great switchback pass into the second chicane to earn seventh position.

Lap 16 and Goethe was back through on Stenshorne, using DRS to get alongside and ahead under braking into Turn 1 for P3.

Roman Bilinski was left on the side of the track after a spin on the exit of Ascari which brought out the Safety Car on Lap 17.

With the DAMS Lucas Oil car cleared away, racing got back underway heading into Lap 20 of 21, and Duerksen retained the lead across the line.

Behind them, León secured fourth from Stenshorne at the first corner, going around the outside of the Rodin driver. Teammate Tsolov followed at the first Lesmo but had lost touch and fallen out of DRS range to the Mexican ahead.

Onto the final lap and the Norwegian driver attempted a pass, but out-braked himself and cut across the chicane. He allowed Tsolov back through ahead of Turn 4 to settle back into sixth.

Having controlled the Safety Car restart, Duerksen had bolted and escaped DRS range for an untroubled run to the line and Sprint Race victory.

Bennett secured second for TRIDENT ahead of Goethe in third for MP Motorsport. León’s charge was rewarded with fourth ahead of teammate Tsolov, Rodin teammates Stenshorne and Dunne, while Laurens van Hoepen completed the points in eighth to make it a double-score for TRIDENT.

KEY QUOTE – Joshua Duerksen, Invicta Racing

“I had an amazing start and the car was just great. I felt very good and had good pace. I really love this track and thank God we could get this win. I’m so happy because it’s an amazing track and I think it’s the best podium of the whole season. I’m very happy and looking forward to tomorrow as well.”

THE CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Nikola Tsolov remains at the head of the Drivers’ Championship with 171 points to his name. Gabriele Minì is P2 on 147 points, two ahead of Rafael Câmara third with 145. Alexander Dunne remains fourth with 110 and Noel León rounds out the top five with 99.

Campos Racing retain their advantage in the Teams’ Standings, now on 270 points. Invicta Racing move onto 198 points with MP Motorsport third on 182. Rodin Motorsport are fourth with 172 points ahead of ART Grand Prix in fifth on 147.

UP NEXT

All eyes turn to Sunday’s Feature Race, with Rafael Câmara set to go from pole position with Invicta Racing teammate Joshua Duerksen alongside him on the front row. Lights out scheduled for 09:45 local time.

title: FIA Formula 2 Championship 2027 Car Launch Press Conference
excerpt:
Q: Welcome to our FIA Formula 2 2027 car reveal press conference, following the launch a moment ago, which was attended by reigning World Champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. We’re joined by the FIA F2 CEO Bruno Michel and Nicolas Tombazis, the FIA’s Single-Seater Director. A very warm welcome to you both. Bruno, if we could start with you, please tell us about the goals behind this new car?

Bruno Michel: Well, the mission of Formula 2 has always been to prepare drivers for Formula 1 and to make sure that when they get into Formula 1, they are ready. So, of course, the car plays a very important role in this preparation. And what we’re always trying to do, because we are making a new car generally every three years, a completely new car or an upgrade of the existing car, we’re trying to get as close as possible to what Formula 1 is at this very stage, to make sure that the drivers are going to be ready when they jump into Formula 1. And that goes not only with the car, but also with the tyres, because we’re using the same supplier, the same partner as Formula 1, with many other subjects of the car. But we are trying to make sure that the drivers are getting as ready as possible.

Q: OK, thank you. Nikolas let’s come to you. Technically, how different is the 2027 car?

Nikolas Tombazis: This car is actually a significant upgrade over the previous car. So, without answering your question directly, there are a lot of similarities to the previous one, a lot of commonalities for cost reasons and to maintain the financial sustainability of the sport, which is always a priority. With that said, there are some very significant changes on the aerodynamics. As Bruno said, there has been a desire to align much more with the Formula 1 philosophy, so all aerodynamics are new, and I think that will guarantee an even better ability to follow closely other cars, not that this is a problem in Formula 2 in general. And I would say there’s also the starter motor, which has been added. That is, again, another important feature in order to avoid, from a sporting point of view, having stalled cars around the track and interrupting the flow of races because of that. The car does have more downforce. I think it’s about 25 points of downforce and a bit more drag, three points. So, it’s fundamentally a much more efficient car dynamically, as well as having better characteristics for following other cars and being more similar to Formula 1, and hence a better proving ground for drivers learning, going up the ladder to get into Formula 1.

Q: How complicated has it been to introduce the starter motor specifically?

Tombazis : It’s obviously an important project. I don’t think it’s an engineering miracle. It’s just there’s been the desire to spend some time and some weight, but the extra weight of that is more than compensated with the better aerodynamics.

Q: Thank you. Bruno, if we come back to you, the car has already tested in Hungary back in June. What feedback did you get from the driver, Paul Aron?

Michel: Well, we had very positive feedback because the good thing with Paul is that he’s been driving the former car as well, so he could have a very interesting comparison between the two cars. And he said that it was very pleasant to drive. He said that you could tell definitely that there was more downforce in this car, that, as Nicolas said, the little additional weight that you got because of the onboard starter, you couldn’t feel it at all, and that he thought that the races were going to be very interesting. Now, as long as we don’t have 22 cars on the track together, we don’t know. But we’re quite confident, with all the work that’s been done aerodynamically between the FIA and ourselves, that we will have a very beautiful car to race.

Q: And what are the plans for the rollout of the new car? When will the teams start to receive the car?

Michel: We’re continuing testing the car. We’ll take the car in the wind tunnel because what we want also is to centralise all the information from the 100% wind tunnel to pass the information to the teams, so they will get all the data so that they don’t have to do it themselves. And then the idea is that the first car will be delivered at the end of the year to the teams, and the second car sometime at the end of January. And then we’ll go testing with 22 cars, because it’s always different when you have a test with one car and when you have a test with 22 cars. And then the cars will be ready to fly to the first race for next season.

title: FIA Formula 2 unveils its new car for the 2027-2029 seasons
excerpt:
Today, FIA Formula 2 presented its new challenger for the 2027, 2028, and 2029 FIA F2 seasons during a special unveiling in the Formula 1 paddock at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza.

Building on the success of the current generation, the F2 2027 car represents a significant evolution designed to further strengthen the Championship’s role as the final step on the pathway to Formula 1.

The car retains the 2026 Dallara chassis to help manage costs, but features redesigned front and rear wings. The improved aerodynamic characteristics will enable closer racing and enhance the drivers’ ability to closely follow the car ahead, while the styling brings it closer to the latest F1 design philosophy.

Powering the car is the proven 3.4-litre turbo-charged Mecachrome engine, which continues to run on advanced sustainable fuel supplied by Aramco, first successfully introduced to the series in 2025. Pirelli, F2’s exclusive tyre supplier since 2017, will continue to provide tyres specifically developed for the championship.

One of the key technical evolutions introduced for the 2027 generation is the addition of an on-board starter. To accommodate this feature, Hewland has developed an evolution of the current gearbox, enabling the integration of the on-board starter system.

The F2 2027 car retains the FIA’s 2024 specifications for braking performance, steering effort and cockpit ergonomics, ensuring the car remains accessible to a broad range of drivers. The Marelli electronic and hydraulic systems package also remain the same, including the EM Motorsport Marshalling system.

His Excellency, Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said: "Formula 2 is where the next generation of top drivers are made. The new 2027 car raises the bar on safety, delivers closer racing, improves accessibility, and reinforces our commitment to sustainability.

“Developed with Formula 2 and our technical partners, this car is designed to push young drivers and prepare them for the highest level of competition, while providing fans with even better racing. It is a key step in strengthening the FIA's single-seater pathway and developing the champions of tomorrow."

Stefano Domenicali, President & CEO of Formula 1, said: “Formula 2 is the ultimate proving ground for the next generation of Formula 1 drivers, where the very best young talent competes wheel-to-wheel and develops the skills needed to reach the pinnacle of motorsport. This new car is another important step forward, combining innovation, safety and closer racing while maintaining the level playing field that allows drivers to showcase their ability. I want to thank His Excellency Mohammed Ben Sulayem and the FIA, Bruno Michel and his team, plus all the technical partners and teams whose collaboration has made this possible. We look forward to seeing the car on the grid, and watching this talented generation create their own stories as they fight for the opportunity to make their mark in Formula 1.”

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 2 Championship CEO, said: “When working on this new car, our first goal was to ensure it remains the perfect tool to prepare drivers for F1. Together with the FIA, we have opted for the current chassis and focused on redesigning the front and the rear wings. This enables us to keep the costs managed, while bringing the design closer to the look of an F1 car while enhancing the F2 car’s ability to deliver close racing.

“We have added an on-board starter that will simplify the operational side for the teams and will allow the drivers to restart their car after spinning or stalling on track, and we’ve been continuing our work with our partners Aramco and Pirelli on driver preparation, sustainability, and providing the fans with a great show.

“Our fans expect the F2 races to be highly entertaining and safe, and this new kit will deliver exactly that.”

The new F2 2027 car fully complies with the latest FIA safety standards, continuing F2’s commitment to providing the highest levels of driver protection while preparing young talent for the demands of Formula 1.

The 2027 car first hit the track at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya last June and has since undergone an intensive development programme jointly with Dallara, including wind tunnel and aero tests.

A first kit will be delivered to the Teams in December 2026, with the second kit to be delivered in January 2027.

The 2027 FIA Formula 2 car – DETAILS

Dimensions

Overall length: 5284 mm Overall width: 1900 mm Overall height: 1097 mm (including FOM roll hoop camera) Wheelbase: 3135 mm

Engine

V6 - 3.4 litre single turbo charged Mecachrome engine. Rated to 620 HP @ 8750 rpm. Fly by wire accelerator system. Rebuild after 8000 km. Maximum Torque 570 Nm @ 6000 rpm.

Monocoque and Bodywork

Survival cell - Sandwich Carbon/aluminium honeycomb structure/Zylon anti-intrusion panels made by Dallara. Front and rear wing - Carbon structures made by Dallara. Bodywork - Carbon - Kevlar honeycomb structures made by Dallara.

title: Several drivers penalised following Monza Qualifying
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of Friday’s FIA Formula 2 Qualifying in Monza, several drivers have been handed penalties.

Firstly, Gabriele Minì has been given a three-place grid penalty for impeding.

Minì was summoned to the stewards after allegedly impeding AIX Racing driver Cian Shields during the session.

After hearing from both drivers, along with their respective team representatives, the Stewards determined that Minì had unnecessarily impeded Shields between Turns 9 to 11, breaching Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

As a result, they elected to hand Minì a three-place grid penalty for both the Sprint and Feature Race.

Secondly, Mari Boya has a three-place grid penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly.

The Stewards examined the available data and spoke to both the driver and a PREMA Racing team representative and found that the driver of Car 12 had slowed significantly on the exit of Turn 10 and began warming its tyres.

The Stewards found that Boya had dropped to an excessively low speed without a valid sporting or safety justification, with the sole purpose of this action being to seek a sporting advantage.

By doing so, Car 12 contributed to the formation of a queue of cars travelling at a very low speed, and this led to incidents involving multiple cars approaching Turn 11.

As a result, they elected to hand Boya a three-place grid penalty for both Monza races.

In addition to that, DAMS Lucas Oil’s Dino Beganovic, Campos Racing’s Noel León, PREMA Racing’s Sebastián Montoya and ART Grand Prix driver Kush Maini have been handed three-place grid penalties for their part in the incident on the approach to Turn 11 towards the end of Qualifying.

The Stewards examined the available data and spoke to all drivers and their team representatives before determining that these four drivers had failed to follow the Race Director Competition Notes, Item 18 Practice and Qualifying Etiquette.

This states that the “drivers not on a fast lap must make all efforts to keep off the racing line’ and “at no point during Practice/Qualifying should drivers remain side-by-side”.

The Stewards found these drivers, while on a preparation lap, drove slowly in the middle of the track between Turn 10 and Turn 11, and remained side-by-side with another car which was not on the racing line.

As a result, Beganovic, Montoya, Maini and León have been given three-place grid penalties to be served in both Monza races.

Lastly, Campos Racing’s Nikola Tsolov has been given a three-place grid penalty for weaving in an erratic manner, close to Car 11 of Sebastián Montoya.

The Stewards examined video evidence and spoke to both drivers and a team representative.

Having considered the matter extensively, they determined that Car 6 was driving erratically by warming its tyres on the racing line, while not travelling at racing speed.

As a result, Montoya was forced to take avoiding action and leave the track. The Stewards therefore imposed a three-place grid penalty on Tsolov to be served in both Monza races.

title: FIA Formula 2 Post-Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following Qualifying here at Monza. Joining us in P3, from Rodin Motorsport is Alexander Dunne; in second place from Invicta Racing is Joshua Dürksen; and also from Invicta Racing, capturing his fifth pole of the season, is Rafael Câmara. Rafa, congratulations. Your fifth pole of the season. How does that feel?

Rafael Câmara: Yes, I'm happy with that. Coming back from the summer break and starting on the right foot is good. I think it was a good lap on the first run. The second run was a bit messier, with some traffic, so I aborted the lap. But the first lap was good enough to put us there, so I'm very happy. Also, with P1 and P2 for the team and Joshua in P2, I think it was a great result on our return. Obviously, we know what Monza is like, so we just need to make sure we keep it clean for the races.

FIA Formula 2: The track temperature was quite high when you were out during the session. Were the tyres tricky at all?

Câmara: Monza is normally a low-energy circuit, so when it's hot, I would say it makes it a bit easier for us. Tyre warm-up is better and you can get the tyres ready for that first lap. On that side, it was not bad. The tyres may have been a bit peakier, but I didn't have any problems, so it was nice.

FIA Formula 2: Was it challenging to find track position today, and how powerful was the tow?

Câmara: It's always tricky because, here in Monza, you always want to look for the tow. I think it's difficult to get pole position here without being in clean air, so I needed to be in a good position. We managed that well on the first run. You're always looking, though. On the second run, everyone was slowing down before Parabolica and trying to get the tow. I think we managed it well today, and it gives us a good place to start on Sunday.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on the pole position, Rafa. Joshua, coming to you, congratulations on P2. Can you take me through your lap?

Joshua Dürksen: I think it was quite a good lap. I usually feel very good in Monza and have very good memories here. The Invicta car is always very good in qualifying, so it gives you a very good feeling straight away and you feel confident and comfortable. It was a good lap. On the second set, it was maybe a bit tricky at the first chicane because everybody slowed down so much before starting the lap. I think the tyres cooled down a little, so there was a bit of an offset. By the second chicane, the tyres were coming back into an optimal temperature window, and it was fine for the rest of the lap. I was pushing hard and came very close to going off several times, but I think it was good because I extracted everything from the car on that lap.

FIA Formula 2: With your P2, that's an Invicta Racing front-row lockout. What does that mean to you and the team?

Dürksen: I think it's the best result you can give the team. They deserve it because they work extremely hard every weekend to give us a very good car, which they do. I think it's the best thing they can see: both cars on the front row. They're very happy, and I'm happy that we could do it here in Monza as well.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P2. Alex, coming to you, the field looked really tight today, with a tenth separating you from pole position. Can you take me through your lap?

Alexander Dunne: It was a difficult one. With all the traffic and chaos while starting the lap and going into the last corner, it was always going to be difficult. Tyre temperatures and getting everything into the right window were quite tricky, but I think we made the most of what was always going to be a difficult situation. I would have liked a little more, but it's nice to be back in the top three after a difficult weekend in Hungary.

FIA Formula 2: Can you take me through the end there? There was a whole group of cars trying to get track position. Was it tough?

Dunne: Yes, it was tricky. I think it was Roman Bilinski who started the chain reaction, when everyone began pushing and stopped driving slowly off the racing line. I had people going around me on the left and right. I just wanted to stay out of trouble, keep my nose clean, and avoid any silly incidents that would make life difficult for the rest of the weekend. I tried to let everyone pass and then went when I felt I was behind someone who would put me in a good position. It was difficult to manage, but I think we ended up okay.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P3, Alex.

title: Noel León: ‘We can fight with the pace we have’ after top five in Monza Qualifying
excerpt:
Noel León wound up fourth in what was a tricky and unpredictable Qualifying session around Monza. The Campos Racing driver was in and around the top spots throughout and was happy with P4 at the chequered flag.

León had held provisional pole early on in the session, and despite slipping down the order by the end, was happy to be fighting at the sharp end which leaves him in a strong position going into the remainder of the weekend.

"Quite happy to be honest. We knew it was going to be a chaotic quali, so we tried to secure a good first lap, which we did and it was P2, so quite happy with what we got.

“P4 is a good position for both races. Pace was good throughout the day right from the start of FP so it was a very good day to be honest.”

Diving deeper into his qualifying session, León says he was happy with his pace overall and it was a tricky time managing the traffic.

He says that the team managed well to get him into a strong position going into each of his flying laps, and that it paid off with a top five result that leaves him in contention for points in both the Sprint and Feature Race.

The Campos driver is very happy with his recent Qualifying form and hopes to convert that into points again this weekend

“After the first push I was P1, then we got some traffic, in a bad place at a bad moment. So yeah, quite happy with the overall pace with the car and the team did an amazing job. So now I’m really looking forward to the races.

"It’s always difficult to get the best track position. Then it was very close with other people because they were driving very slow at the end. But I think it is what it is, and we knew this was going to happen, so we tried our best and we ended up top five. Really happy that it played out.”

His strong Monza qualifying follows on from a top three result in Budapest prior to the summer break.

READ MORE

QUALIFYING: Camara leads Invicta 1-2 in Monza

The Mexican driver says his uptick in form particularly on a single lap has been a big confidence boost heading into the upcoming phase of the season and a busy September.

He will now be looking to maximise his results in what he says will be “chaotic” races given the layout of the Monza circuit and the additional DRS zone added for 2026.

"I feel good to be honest. I know what I need to work on to be better. But still, two very good qualifying sessions back-to-back. Budapest was P3 and now P4. So we're in the mix and we can have a great time. I'm looking forward to the races.

"It's going to be difficult. There is a new DRS zone which means it's going to be difficult to be out of DRS range and it will be important to manage the tyres because it's quite hot and it's going to be an issue. It's going to be chaotic, and we'll try to stay out of trouble.”

title: QUALIFYING: Camara leads Invicta 1-2 in Monza
excerpt:
Rafael Câmara secured pole position for Invicta Racing by less than a tenth over teammate Joshua Duerksen. The Brazilian delivered a 1:31.326 on his penultimate attempt and nobody could beat him to the Aramco Pole Position Award. Alexander Dunne completed the top three for Rodin Motorsport.

Dunne was fastest in Practice but his first effort was undone by a lock-up into the Ascari chicane that sent him skipping across the gravel, leaving him to regroup for his next attempt.

Noel León set the provisionally fastest lap but that was beaten by Duerksen with a 1:31.707 to put the Invicta driver ahead of the Mexican by just under two-tenths.

Dunne launched into a second attempt on his first set of Supersofts but went deep into Turn 1, and he abandoned his lap once more.

León found an improvement but this time it was the Invicta of Câmara that demoted him from top spot, with the Brazilian setting a 1:31.326 to go provisionally fastest.

Duerksen and Nikola Tsolov followed their teammates in third and fourth respectively at the halfway stage, with Oliver Goethe and Gabriele Minì fifth and sixth for MP Motorsport.

Dunne went for a third attempt on his first set of tyres and he delivered a time good enough to go fourth without a tow for the majority of his lap.

Drivers returned to the circuit on fresh tyres with just over five minutes remaining of the session for their final flying laps.

The majority opted to run through the pit lane in order to get ideal track position and gain a tow, though several remained on circuit including Championship leader Tsolov in a separate smaller group of cars headed by PREMA Racing’s Mari Boya.

Roman Bilinski passed everyone and he launched into his final attempt at the front of the queue, while there was plenty of squabbling for position behind him with less than a minute to go.

Martinius Stenshorne went up to third for Rodin Motorsport while teammate Dunne found a time good enough for second, but was subsequently demoted to P3 by Duerksen.

It left Invicta 1-2 on the grid with Câmara on pole. León was fourth ahead of Stenshorne who wound up fifth.

Tsolov finished up sixth ahead of Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak, Ritomo Miyata, Oliver Goethe and John Bennett in the top 10.

The FIA Formula 2 Sprint Race around Monza is scheduled to get underway at 14:15 local time on Saturday, with the Briton set to go from reverse grid pole.

title: Rodin’s pace ‘nice to see’ says Dunne after topping Monza Free Practice
excerpt:
Alexamder Dunne has been reflecting on his Monza Free Practice after setting the fastest time of the session

Alexander Dunne was fastest in this morning’s Monza Free Practice, and while he was happy with his pace, he was slightly surprised by the gap to the rest of the field.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was in good form on Formula 2’s return from the summer break, consistently finding himself at the top of the timesheets after each lap.

Dunne completed a 1:31.957 with his final attempt of the Red Flag curtailed session, a time that was quick enough to lead MP Motorsport’s Oliver Goethe by 0.170s.

But it was the 0.506s gap to Nico Varrone in third that caught the Irishman’s eye, although he does not expect that to be the case come Qualifying.

“It's a good way to start,” said Dunne. “It's only Free Practice, so it doesn't really mean a whole lot, but the pace was good.

“I'm quite surprised by the gap from me to P3, that it was half a second. But then from P3 to P10 was two tenths, which is more what you would expect.

Dunne ended up with the fastest time in the Monza Free Practice

“It's nice to see that we have a good amount of pace, but I imagine it's going to get a lot closer. I don't expect it to be that comfortable in quali.

“There's a couple of things we can improve on, but I'm sure the other teams will find some stuff that they can do better for quali as well, and we're on a different compound.

“We didn't get to do many laps, but the laps that we did do were good ones. So it was fun.”

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Dunne quickest for Rodin Motorsport after Red Flag curtails Monza opener

Gabriele Minì: ‘We can close the gap down but have to maximise in Qualifying’

While the change from the Softs to Supersofts is expected to be a major factor, the battle for track position could be as well, with drivers looking to find a tow ahead of their laps.

There was plenty of jostling for places during Free Practice, but Dunne was happy to have avoided it, and to have kept his session clean.

“It wasn't too bad,” he said of the traffic in the session. “I was in a good place on track, so I avoided all the chaos and the mess, and I just got to do my own thing and focus on driving rather than getting stuck in a car park in a traffic jam.

The Rodin driver is hoping for a clean qualifying later today

“So, it was good. I'm happy, the car felt really good, and I felt like I was driving well as well. Usually, most of the time, when we put those two things together, the end result is pretty good. So, if we can have a good quali, that'd be nice.”

When asked what the keys will be for Qualifying, Dunne responded: “I think it's just to have a good tow, but you need to have a good tow behind someone who is fast.

READ MORE

The Formula 2 stars past and present set to take part in FP1 at the Italian Grand Prix

PREVIEW: A return to action at the Temple of Speed

“If you put yourself behind someone who is a second off, you're going to be in trouble by the end of the lap. So, I think finding yourself in a good position with a strong tow behind someone who can keep the pace up through the lap as well so that you don't find yourself in a difficult position come the end of the lap.

“This is what we managed to do pretty well on all three push laps that I had today. We were all in the right track position, which is nice. So, I think we've prepped ourselves well for quali and we know where we need to go, which is nice.”

Next Up

title: PRACTICE: Dunne quickest for Rodin Motorsport after Red Flag curtails Monza opener
excerpt:
Alexander Dunne topped the timing screens for Rodin Motorsport, with the Irishman in and around the top spots from the green light before eventually ending up P1 with a 1:31.957.

After a quiet start, Emerson Fittipaldi put the first time on the board with a 1:34.793 for AIX Racing.

As the clock ticked beneath half an hour to go, more times arrived and Noel León went fastest on a 1:32.715 for Campos Racing, 0.3s clear of Martinius Stenshorne of Rodin Motorsport.

Several drivers delivered an improvement on that session-topping time on their next efforts, with Dunne setting a 1:32.297 to go to P1.

Oliver Goethe was next to take over at the top. A 1:32.127 put the MP Motorsport driver fastest but only briefly as Dunne restored himself to the front with a 1:31.957.

With 17 minutes to go, the Red Flags were out after a crash for Colton Herta out of Turn 7. He was out of the car and OK, but the Hitech car needed clearing, with the American having caught the gravel on corner exit, sending him into the inside wall.

There was not enough time to get the session restarted before the clock hit zero, leaving Dunne as the fastest driver ahead of Goethe and Nico Varrone in the top three.

Nikola Tsolov was fourth ahead of Roman Bilinski, Joshua Duerksen, Stenshorne, León, Rafael Camara and Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak in the top 10.

Qualifying gets underway at 14:55 local time on Friday.

title: Gabriele Minì: ‘We can close the gap down but have to maximise in Qualifying’
excerpt:
With the title battle reaching a crucial phase, Gabriele Minì is targeting a big result at his home event around the Autodromo Nazionale Monza.

The Italian is currently second in the standings, 20 points adrift of Championship leader Nikola Tsolov, but is optimistic of closing that gap down this weekend.

Speaking ahead of on-track running, Minì said that the goal would remain the same as always – maximise the results.

“To be honest, you always try to do the best you can, because we're not the ones that are being chased, so there is no need to look at what the others do,” Minì explained.

“We still have to try to do the best result possible and try to close down the gap. Of course, you think about the championship, but you don't want to do anything stupid if your championship rivals are behind you.

“But you still want to maximise what you can. You don't have to play games with the others, that's not the way we have to approach it. We have to try and win, do the best we can as always.

Minì says Qualifying will be the important factor this weekend to avoid any incidents at Turn 1

“Obviously, you go out there in order to win, but the main goal is to catch up. The gap is 20 points at the moment, and I'd say that if you could consistently win, it would be better, right? Hopefully, we can do that too, but consistency is important, you still have to score big points.”

While it isn’t always crucial to start from pole position in F2 around Monza, a strong grid position is important nonetheless.

He says Friday’s Qualifying session will be critical, moreso than usual given the incredibly challenging start around Monza, going into one of the biggest braking zones for Turn 1 on the calendar at one of the tightest chicanes.

READ MORE

PREVIEW: A return to action at the Temple of Speed

LN4 Fusion announces intention to enter FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2027

Keeping out of trouble there will go a long way in improving prospects of a strong result according to the Alpine Academy driver.

“Qualifying is always unique around Monza, because it's such a question mark. So many things can go your way, and at the same time, so many things can go wrong.

“So, you need to take a lot of things into consideration, but qualifying plays a big role. Turn One - we go from a very high speed to a very, very slow speed. Even missing the braking by one metre by a car behind can make a difference for the cars in front.

The Italian is chasing down Tsolov in the title battle and is 20 points adrift heading into the Monza weekend

So, starting in front of the majority of the pack is really important, but it's not something you can control. You just try to stay out of the trouble but you never know where the trouble is going to be.

"It's a bit more instinctive. Can't really plan anything beforehand. But I’m quite confident. I had a break, some time to switch off and then come back ready.

“I'm sure the engineers and everyone have put in quite a lot of work, even myself and the team and the simulator. So, I'm ready, feeling ready and I'm feeling confident.”

With Monza being a home race, Minì is hoping to use some of his experience around the famous venue to good effect.

Overall, the Italian is looking forward to competing on home turf and is hoping to put on a show for his home fans whatever comes.

“Everything is special, I'd say. It's a really good track. It's going to be a chaotic weekend for sure. We have seen in the past, many nice races, a lot of overtakes, a lot of slipstream, and positioning is going to be key.

"So, it's going to be a chaotic one, but it's one of the tracks I know best, and it being my home race, hearing the fans and seeing them there makes all the difference.”

title: The Formula 2 stars past and present set to take part in FP1 at the Italian Grand Prix
excerpt:

title: PREVIEW: A return to action at the Temple of Speed
excerpt:
The summer break is over and the drivers are all set to jump back into their cars for Round 10 of the 2026 FIA Formula 2 season at Monza.

The Temple of Speed has created many iconic moments in championship history, and with the title fight closer than ever, we are set for another incredible weekend of racing in Italy.

With 22 drivers raring to go after the hiatus, here is everything you need to know about the trip to Monza…

WHAT TO EXPECT

The drivers will hit the track for the first time on Friday morning at 10:00 local time for the 45-minute Free Practice outing.

Qualifying follows later in the day at 14:55 local time, the result of this session sets the grid for both Monza races.

The first race of the weekend is on Saturday afternoon with the 21-lap Sprint listed to start at 14:15 local time.

The drivers will get more one more chance to claim glory at the historic Italian venue in the Feature Race. Lights out is scheduled for 09:45 local time on Sunday morning.

In addition to that, the 2027 FIA Formula 2 car is set to be revealed on Saturday morning at 11:30 local time.

FROM THE GRID – John Bennett, TRIDENT

“I’ll describe the Monza weekend as fast, Italian, and passionate. The venue itself is super cool. The Italian fans are always amazing, and now being with an Italian team it will be even cooler.

“On track, the best places to overtake are down the inside or around the outside into Turn 1. If you are around the outside at T1, you can be on the inside at Turn 2. So you go into T1 with DRS, and then you get the overlap into the big braking zone.

“The challenges of Monza are the braking zones, because you've got a low downforce setup on the car, but you are approaching everywhere at super high speeds, and you have to get the braking points right.”

TECHNICAL PREVIEW

Pierre-Alain Michot, FIA Formula 2 Technical Director

“Monza is an incredible venue where three quarters of the lap is spent at full throttle, and with top end speed vital, downforce requirements are low."

“At the end of several of these long straights are heavy braking zones, especially at Turn 1, so braking demands are high, as is fuel consumption.

“The drivers will be eyeing a slipstream in Qualifying but history shows that victory can be achieved outside of the front row, and this often leads to very entertaining races.”

PIRELLI PREVIEW

The two softest compounds in the range have been selected for the race weekend at Monza. Soft and Supersoft will therefore be the available options at one of the fastest circuits on the calendar. In the Feature Race, the theoretically quickest strategy is expected to involve starting on the Supersoft, followed by a pit stop around lap seven and then completing the race on the Soft compound. Tyre degradation at Monza should not be severe enough to compromise the length of the opening stint on the Supersoft. Graining could occur mainly on the front axle, while the rear tyres may be susceptible to overheating due to the frequent traction phases that characterise this circuit. Should track temperatures fail to reach the high expected levels, graining could become the dominant factor in tyre management.

title: LN4 Fusion announces intention to enter FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2027
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion has confirmed its intention to enter the team application process with a view to entry in the FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2027.

The team is co-founded by 2025 Formula 1 World Champion Lando Norris and today confirmed that it acquired selected assets of AIX Racing. It will also undertake application procedures to join the F2 grid next season.

LN4 Fusion also confirmed that Rene Rosin will serve as Team Principal, with Guillaume Capietto serving as Racing Director for the team’s wider operation.

Norris detailed the plans currently in the works along with a driver development programme, having come through FIA Formula 2 himself en route to F1 and winning the World Championship last year.

Co-founder Norris said: “I’ve been really lucky to have some amazing people around me throughout my career, and I know that getting to Formula 1 takes so much more than just talent. You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time.

“That’s what these two projects are all about. LN4 Fusion is about building a race team that can compete with the best in junior motorsport, with great people and a great environment for drivers to develop. The LN4 Legacy Programme is about helping talented young drivers get opportunities they might not otherwise have.

“For me, they naturally fit together. I want to help create opportunities for the next generation, both on and off the track, and hopefully make a real difference to young drivers coming through the sport.”

FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel commented: “I’m very pleased to see that Lando Norris, who is the first F2 graduate to have become a Formula 1 World Champion, is showing interest in getting involved in an F2 team. LN4 Fusion has taken over AIX Racing and will be applying for an entry for the next three-year cycle of Formula 2, which will run from 2027 until 2029.”

Team Principal Rosin added: "Motorsport has always been my passion and my professional life. I am thrilled to have the opportunity to contribute my experience to an independent, vision-driven sporting programme with strong backing, a clear long-term vision and the resources required to build it properly. Having Lando on board adds a further dimension to this project. He has come through the junior single-seater ranks and understands its demands. His involvement will make a real difference to the team.

"We want to develop a pathway through junior single-seaters and create an environment in which drivers, engineers and sporting personnel can perform at the highest level. My role is to focus on racing: building and managing the sporting programme, creating the right technical environment and helping the team become competitive."

title: WHAT TO WATCH FOR: The key storylines post summer break in Monza
excerpt:
The summer break is over which means it is time to return to racing, as the paddock heads to Monza for Round 10 of the 2026 season.

The Temple of Speed is a favourite for many drivers, teams and fans, and with the title fight closer than ever we can expect another fascinating trip to Italy.

But before we hit the track, here are a few storylines to look out for this weekend…

THE TITLE CHASING TRIO

Heading into the weekend, Nikola Tsolov leads the Drivers’ Standings on 167 points with Gabriele Minì and Rafael Câmara just 20 and 22 points behind respectively.

Monza has previously played an integral role in the title fight, such as in 2024 when Gabriel Bortoleto’s championship comeback started with an iconic victory from last in the Feature Race.

Tsolov, Minì and Câmara would rather not tempt fate by starting at the back this weekend, but a strong three days on F2’s return to action could prove vital in the championship battle.

Tsolov and Câmara are strong contenders for the title going into Monza

There are not many rounds left in the season so each point will be vital, and with all three drivers having achieved multiple victories they will be confident of being back on the top step in Monza.

The results this weekend will not decide the title for either of these three, but it could give them the momentum boost they need going into the final part of the season.

READ MORE

How to watch Round 10 in Monza: TV, Session times and more

FORMULA 2’s 10TH SEASON: Lando Norris on how F2 prepared him for Formula 1

A PUNCHER’S CHANCE

For a long time Alexander Dunne had been firmly in the title fight, but he returns to the paddock 59 points behind Tsolov.

The Rodin Motorsport driver still has a chance having had a consistent year, but he hasn't been on the podium since Barcelona.

Last time out in Budapest, damage in Qualifying left him starting down the order in both races, and he did not score a single point.

But Dunne has shown what he is capable of doing in a Formula 2 car and as previously said we have seen title comebacks start in Monza.

Dunne and Beganovic both have an outside chance of claiming the title

The Irish driver will not be the only driver hoping to start their fightback however, as the likes of Noel León, Kush Maini and Dino Beganovic will also be keen to close that gap.

The top three may be far ahead but a lot can happen in Formula 2, and there's still a chance for many drivers, so they will be battling hard in Monza.

DO YOU WANT POLE?

On Formula 2’s previous nine visits to Monza, only twice has the pole-sitter converted that starting position into Feature Race victory.

The first was Oscar Piastri in 2021 and the second was Luke Browning last season.

We have seen Bortoleto win from last, we have also watched Tadasuke Makino take victory from P14, and Mick Schumacher from seventh.

This is to say that the results in Qualifying should not be how the drivers define success this weekend. Piastri and Browning proved you can win from pole, while others showed that you can make a fightback through the field.

Bortoleto won the 2024 Monza Feature Race from the back of the grid

So even if your favourite driver does not take pole on Friday, they are still very much in the running for victory in both races around Monza.

HOME TEAMS EYEING SUCCESS

The drivers will be eyeing victory no doubt, but so will the teams, especially two Italian outfits in the field – TRIDENT and PREMA Racing.

The latter have an incredible record at Monza, having taken seven victories there in Formula 2. This includes a famous double in 2023 when Frederik Vesti won the Sprint and Oliver Bearman claimed Feature Race victory.

READ MORE

Nikola Tsolov completes first F1 test with Racing Bulls

Spielberg victory ‘best day of my life’ after tough couple of seasons says Bennett

TRIDENT on the other hand have not been able to replicate that success but they do have two podiums at the Temple of Speed – Bent Viscaal finished second in 2021 and Richard Verschoor in 2024.

They have shown great pace this year with Laurens van Hoepen and John Bennett, so they will feel they are very much primed for their first win in Monza.

As for PREMA, it has not been the smoothest of years, but there is no better place to get back on track than at home.
